purpose: Dasiglucagon is used to treat very low blood sugar (severe hypoglycemia) in people with diabetes who are 6 years of age and older. It is an emergency medicine used when someone cannot eat or drink to raise their blood sugar on their own. It is given as a quick injection under the skin and works fast to help bring blood sugar back up to a safe level.
how_it_works: Your liver stores sugar in a form called glycogen. When you inject dasiglucagon, it signals your liver to quickly break down that stored sugar and release it into your bloodstream. This causes your blood sugar to rise within minutes, helping you recover from a dangerous low blood sugar episode.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, vomiting, headache, and diarrhea. These usually go away on their own fairly quickly after the injection. Some people may also notice redness, swelling, or mild pain at the injection site.
warnings: After using dasiglucagon, the person should eat a snack or meal as soon as they are able to swallow safely to help keep blood sugar stable. If blood sugar does not improve within 15 minutes, call 911 immediately. It should not be used if someone has a tumor that produces glucagon (glucagonoma) or a tumor of the adrenal gland (pheochromocytoma). Always let your doctor know if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or have any other health conditions.
typical_dosing: For adults and children 6 years and older, the usual dose is 0.6 mg injected just under the skin (subcutaneously), typically in the stomach area, outer thigh, or outer upper arm. It comes as a pre-filled auto-injector pen for easy use in an emergency. Caregivers and family members should be trained ahead of time on how to use it so they are ready if an emergency happens.
